title: Closed-Form Powers of a 2×2 Matrix via the Characteristic Polynomial
description: Makes the abstract Cayley-Hamilton power reduction of the parent entry fully explicit in the 2×2 case. For any 2×2 matrix M over a commutative ring with t = tr M and d = det M, the powers of M are an explicit affine combination of M and the identity: Mⁿ⁺¹ = u(n+1)·M − (d·u(n))·I, where u is the Lucas sequence of the first kind for the characteristic polynomial X²−tX+d (u₀=0, u₁=1, u(k+2)=t·u(k+1)−d·u(k)). Fully general — no diagonalisability or eigenvalue hypotheses. Showcased on the Fibonacci matrix !![1,1;1,0], whose Lucas sequence is the Fibonacci sequence itself. 9 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: That every power of a square matrix is a polynomial of degree below the dimension is the immediate computational corollary of the Cayley-Hamilton theorem (Cayley 1858 for 2×2 and 3×3; Frobenius 1879 in general). In dimension two the reduction is sharpest: the characteristic polynomial X²−tX+d closes the power recursion into a single second-order linear recurrence — a Lucas sequence in the sense of Édouard Lucas (1878), whose first-kind sequences Uₙ generalise the Fibonacci numbers (t=1, d=−1) and the Pell numbers (t=2, d=−1). The identity Mⁿ⁺¹ = U(n+1)·M − d·Uₙ·I is the matrix incarnation of the Lucas-sequence theory and underlies fast exponentiation of 2×2 matrices, the matrix proof of Fibonacci identities (e.g. Cassini's identity from det Mⁿ = (det M)ⁿ), and the closed-form solution of two-term linear recurrences.
overview.problemStatement: The parent entry (cayley-hamilton-oq-02) proves the abstract reduction Aᵏ = (Xᵏ mod χ_A)(A) but leaves the reduced polynomial implicit. Make it fully explicit in the 2×2 case: give a closed form for Mⁿ as an affine combination of M and I with computable scalar coefficients.
overview.text: For a 2×2 matrix M the Cayley-Hamilton theorem reads M² = t·M − d·I with t = tr M and d = det M. Writing Mⁿ⁺¹ = aₙ·M + bₙ·I, multiplying by M and substituting M² collapses the M² term, giving aₙ₊₁ = t·aₙ + bₙ, bₙ₊₁ = −d·aₙ. Eliminating bₙ shows aₙ = u(n+1) and bₙ = −d·u(n) where u is the Lucas sequence u₀=0, u₁=1, u(k+2)=t·u(k+1)−d·u(k). Hence Mⁿ⁺¹ = u(n+1)·M − d·u(n)·I.
overview.proofStrategy: Specialise Cayley-Hamilton to 2×2 via Matrix.charpoly_fin_two and Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly to obtain M² = t·M − d·I (sq_eq_trace_smul_sub_det_smul). Then prove the closed form by a one-step induction on n: at the successor step, write Mⁿ⁺² = M·Mⁿ⁺¹, substitute the inductive closed form, push M through the scalar multiplications, replace M² using the 2×2 Cayley-Hamilton identity, and match scalar coefficients with the Lucas recurrence (match_scalars; ring).
keyInsights: The whole closed form needs only the inductive hypothesis at a single previous step (not two), because multiplying Mⁿ⁺¹ = u(n+1)·M − d·u(n)·I by M produces an M² that the 2×2 Cayley-Hamilton identity immediately reduces — so ordinary induction suffices, no two-step induction is required
The scalar recursion that drops out is exactly the Lucas sequence of the first kind for X²−tX+d; specialising (t,d) recovers Fibonacci (1,−1), Pell (2,−1), and Chebyshev-like families

The result holds over any commutative (nontrivial) ring R, not just fields — the proof uses only Cayley-Hamilton and ring arithmetic, never eigenvalues or diagonalisability, so it applies to integer and polynomial matrices
Taking determinants of the closed form (det Mⁿ = dⁿ) recovers Fibonacci/Lucas identities such as Cassini's identity Fₙ₊₁Fₙ₋₁ − Fₙ² = (−1)ⁿ as the n-th power of det of the Fibonacci matrix

match_scalars reduces the matrix identity to two scalar identities in the free R-module on {M, I}, after which the Lucas recurrence closes the goal by ring — a clean separation of the linear-algebraic and the recurrence content
prerequisites: Cayley-Hamilton theorem (Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly) and the 2×2 characteristic polynomial X²−(tr M)X+(det M)
Second-order linear recurrences (Lucas sequences of the first kind)
Scalar multiplication in the ring of matrices over a commutative ring

conclusion.summary: 9 theorems, 2 definitions, 132 lines, 0 axioms, 0 sorries. An explicit closed form for the powers of any 2×2 matrix over any commutative ring: Mⁿ⁺¹ = u(n+1)·M − (det M · u n)·I, with u the Lucas sequence of the characteristic polynomial. The 2×2 Cayley-Hamilton identity M² = (tr M)·M − (det M)·I is derived from Mathlib, the closed form by a one-step induction, and the Fibonacci matrix is given as a worked showcase where the Lucas recursion is the Fibonacci recurrence.
conclusion.implications: This is the explicit, computable specialisation of the parent's abstract power reduction. It turns Mⁿ into an O(log n) computation by fast exponentiation of the scalar Lucas pair, gives a uniform matrix derivation of identities for any two-term linear recurrence (Fibonacci, Pell, Lucas numbers), and—via det Mⁿ = (det M)ⁿ—delivers Cassini-type identities for free. It is the n=2 base case of a hierarchy whose general step is the parent's modByMonic reduction.
